  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(\n    input [7:0] address,\n    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,\n    input [7:0] b,\n    input control,\n    output [15:0] count\n);\n\n    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;\n\n    wire [7:0] offset1, offset2;\n    wire [15:0] addr_sum;\n    wire [15:0] count1, count2;\n\n    assign offset1 = base - ptr1;\n    assign offset2 = base - ptr2;\n    assign addr_sum = {8'h00, address} + {8'h00, b};\n    assign count1 = addr_sum - {8'h00, offset1};\n    assign count2 = addr_sum - {8'h00, offset2};\n    assign count = (control == 1'b1) ? count1 : count2;\n\nendmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The likely mapped bottleneck is the per-branch arithmetic depth before the final control mux: an 8-bit offset subtract followed by a 16-bit address-minus-offset operation and a separate 16-bit addition. The RTL dependency graph shows that the address-plus-b term is common to both branches, while the supplied mapping flow allows Yosys/ABC to restructure the arithmetic, so this is a timing hypothesis rather than proof of the final cell topology. OpenSTA on the mapped candidate is required to confirm the critical path.",
  "rewrite": "Form the common 16-bit address-plus-b sum once, then subtract the selected branch's zero-extended, exactly 8-bit-truncated offset. This removes the duplicated 16-bit addition from the two branch paths while retaining the late control mux and avoiding placing control in front of the arithmetic. The modulo-65536 associativity of addition and subtraction makes this equivalent to the original sequence after the mandatory 8-bit offset truncation.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to provide a modest reduction in maximum data arrival if the baseline contains distinct per-branch adders after the address subtraction. The final result mux and the offset subtracts remain, so the gain is not guaranteed; fixed-flow synthesis, mapping, and OpenSTA must establish the actual result.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Likely reduced or approximately unchanged mapped area because one common 16-bit adder replaces two branch-local 16-bit adders. The shared adder may increase fanout on its result, so mapped area, buffering, slew, and capacitance must still be checked against the stated cap and zero-violation requirements.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, parameter declaration, and default base value are unchanged. offset1 and offset2 remain 8-bit expressions, preserving truncation modulo 256. Each result is computed modulo 65536, and control=1 selects ptr1/count1 while every other control value selects ptr2/count2. All address, ptr1, ptr2, b, control, and parameter-instance behavior remains unconstrained except for the stated default-instance assessment; no clocks, state, assumptions, input restrictions, or don't-cares are introduced."
